title: SharePoint: Agent Chat web part embeds Microsoft 365 Copilot agents in pages
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout dates, user requirements and existing agent-blocking control are supported. Three minor wording corrections would distinguish what Microsoft explicitly states from what its documentation does not describe.

claims.claim: Agent Chat is a new web part for modern SharePoint page editors.
claims.quote: This is a new web part available for modern page editors in SharePoint.

claims.claim: The roadmap says the web part can be configured to use any Microsoft 365 Copilot agent.
claims.quote: The web part can be configured to use any M365 Copilot agent.

claims.claim: Organizations can embed existing Microsoft 365 Copilot agents in SharePoint pages.
claims.quote: We're introducing the Agent Chat web part in SharePoint, allowing organizations to embed their existing Microsoft 365 Copilot agents directly into SharePoint pages.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Who and where
claims.claim: SharePoint Online page authors add the web part using the standard page editing experience.
claims.quote: Platforms/Services: SharePoint Online, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft Copilot Studio. What will happen: SharePoint page authors can add the Agent Chat web part to pages using the standard page editing experience.

claims.claim: Authors select agents that are already published.
claims.quote: Authors can select published agents already available to them in Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: The selected agent must already be available to the author in Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: Authors can select published agents already available to them in Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Users interact with the agent directly from a SharePoint page.
claims.quote: Users can interact with agents directly from SharePoint pages and continue conversations in a full-screen chat experience.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Users can continue the conversation in a full-screen chat experience.
claims.quote: Users can interact with agents directly from SharePoint pages and continue conversations in a full-screen chat experience.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance

claims.quote: Existing SharePoint page permissions and agent access permissions remain independent.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Adding an agent to a page does not automatically grant users access to that agent.
claims.quote: Adding an agent to a page does not automatically grant users access to that agent.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: SharePoint page content is not automatically passed to the agent.
claims.quote: SharePoint page content is not automatically passed to the agent.

claims.quote: SharePoint does not store Copilot agent chat data or change how agent data is processed.

claims.claim: SharePoint does not change how agent data is processed.
claims.quote: SharePoint does not store Copilot agent chat data or change how agent data is processed.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; summary; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale
claims.claim: The notice names users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence and access to the configured agent, supporting per-user entitlement.
claims.quote: Who is affected: SharePoint page authors who want to embed Copilot agents. Users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and access to the configured agent.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The notice names page authors who want to embed Copilot agents as affected.
claims.quote: Who is affected: SharePoint page authors who want to embed Copilot agents.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; rationale: risk and impact; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The capability is user-opt-in: authors choose to add it, with no documented web-part-specific admin enablement switch.
claims.quote: Searched: 'SharePoint "Agent Chat" web part disable admin identity license pricing'; 'SharePoint "Agent Chat" "web part" "DisabledWebPartIds"'. Read MC1559633, Manage access to agents in SharePoint and Set-SPOTenant; authors add the part and no specific enablement switch was found.

claims.claim: No Microsoft Learn page describing the Agent Chat web part was found.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Agent Chat web part" SharePoint'; '"Agent Chat" SharePoint "identity" "disable" "pricing"'. Results describe surrounding agents or unrelated chat products; read Manage access to agents in SharePoint, agent-actions, authentication and billing pages, none describing this web part.

claims.claim: An agent's configured capabilities define the scope of its accessible knowledge sources.
claims.quote: The Agent Capabilities section displays the configured capabilities for the agent, defining the scope of its accessible knowledge sources.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not described which identity this web part uses when calling the agent or its sign-in experience.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Agent Chat web part" authentication sign in identity'. Read MC1559633 and Configure user authentication in Copilot Studio; the latter describes agent authentication in SharePoint generally, not this web part's calling identity or sign-in experience.

claims.claim: The notice does not describe an approval step added by the web part.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Agent Chat" SharePoint "approval"'. Read MC1559633 in full and the returned Publish an agent to SharePoint excerpt; the notice describes published-agent selection and chat, not a web-part approval step.

claims.claim: The notice states no admin switch for the web part.
claims.quote: Searched: 'SharePoint "Agent Chat" web part disable admin identity license pricing'; '"Agent Chat web part" block Copilot admin'. Read MC1559633, agent-actions, Manage access to agents in SharePoint and Set-SPOTenant. No web-part-specific switch found; the notice says no admin action is required.
claims.fix: Replace 'the notice states no admin switch for it' with 'the notice says no admin action is required before rollout'. The notice does not explicitly say that no switch exists.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No price, credit rate or meter specific to the web part is published.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Agent Chat web part" license meter cost'. Read MC1559633, Licensing for agents powered by the standard harness and Meters for Microsoft Copilot pay-as-you-go services. General agent billing is described, but none names a price or meter specific to the web part.
claims.fix: In the cost rationale, replace 'and states no separate meter or price for the web part' with 'and no price or meter specific to the web part was found in Microsoft documentation at the time of writing (November 2026)'. This distinguishes a confirmed absence from an explicit Microsoft statement.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio documents billing conditions for agents used in SharePoint.
claims.quote: If you have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, using agents in Copilot Chat, Microsoft Teams, or SharePoint for classic answers, generative answers, or Microsoft Graph tenant grounding isn't charged when the agent runs with your authenticated identity.

claims.claim: The agent-blocking path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > All agents. ... In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents. ... In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select Block or Unblock.

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package to prevent usage.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: Agent blocking is an existing tenant-wide control.
claims.quote: Block or unblock agents for the entire organization by using the same controls that work for any other app in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Blocking agents created in SharePoint or Foundry affects Microsoft Copilot Chat only.
claims.quote: However, blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: The block API is available in the Global service.
claims.quote: | Global service | US Government L4 | US Government L5 (DOD) | China operated by 21Vianet | ... | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |

claims.claim: The block API is not supported in US Government L4.
claims.quote: | Global service | US Government L4 | US Government L5 (DOD) | China operated by 21Vianet | ... | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |

claims.claim: The block API is not supported in US Government L5 (DOD).
claims.quote: | Global service | US Government L4 | US Government L5 (DOD) | China operated by 21Vianet | ... | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |

claims.claim: The block API is not supported in China operated by 21Vianet.
claims.quote: | Global service | US Government L4 | US Government L5 (DOD) | China operated by 21Vianet | ... | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |

claims.claim: The Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: The block API operation is a preview operation.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not state whether blocking also removes the agent from this web part.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Agent Chat web part" block Copilot admin'. Read agent-actions, copilotPackage: block and Manage access to agents in SharePoint. Host availability effects are documented, including SharePoint-created agents' Chat-only blocking; removal from this web part is not described.

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant has a -DisabledWebPartIds parameter.
claims.quote: ### -DisabledWebPartIds ... Allows administrators to prevent certain web parts from being added to pages or rendering on pages on which they were previously added.

claims.where: Governance controls: Set-SPOTenant paragraph; Open questions
claims.claim: No page found states that -DisabledWebPartIds covers Agent Chat or gives its web part ID.
claims.quote: Searched: 'SharePoint "Agent Chat" "web part" "DisabledWebPartIds"'. Read and searched Set-SPOTenant for DisabledWebPartIds, Agent Chat and AgentChat. Its supported list includes Amazon Kindle, YouTube, Twitter, Embed, Microsoft Bookings and Stream only; no Agent Chat ID found.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence beginning 'The Set-SPOTenant reference lists' with 'The Set-SPOTenant reference documents -DisabledWebPartIds for Amazon Kindle, YouTube, Twitter, Embed, Microsoft Bookings and Stream only; it does not list Agent Chat.' The reference explicitly restricts the supported web parts.

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified at 2026-10-13T23:01:05.
Microsoft Learn documents no setting named specifically for this web part.
claims.quote: Searched: 'SharePoint "Agent Chat" web part disable admin identity license pricing'; 'SharePoint "Agent Chat" "web part" "DisabledWebPartIds"'; '"Agent Chat web part" block Copilot admin'. Read Set-SPOTenant, Manage access to agents in SharePoint and agent-actions; no named setting found.
